main_text.l: SI Christus pro nobis, pro peccatis nostris, propter peccata nostra, est vulneratus, attritus, passus, & deniq; mortuus, ita, ut prapositi-ones illa, PRO & PROPTER, indicent, & causam finalem, & efficientem impulsivam, ita nimirum, ut in finali causa intelligamus satisfactionem, in efficiente impulsiva Imputationem: Utiq; Christus patiendo & moriendo pro nobis judicio Dei satisfecit, & poenas peccatis nostris debitas exsolvit.

Atqui Christus pro nobis, pro peccatis nostris, propter peccata nostra, in S. literis dicitur vulneratus, attritus, passus & deniq; mortuus. Sed parumper subsistamus, & audiamus alios, qui fatentur, &, ut dicunt, in Deo suo gloriantur, Jesum Christum, Dei Filium, propter iniquitates nostras, & pro peccatis nostris, ut universa sacra Scriptura testatur, mortuum esse: sed inde tamen consequi constanter negant, Christum Dei judicio pro peccatis nostris satisfecisse, sive illi id solvisse, quod nos propter peccata nostra solvere debuissemus. Mori enim propter peccata, inquiunt illi, seu pro peccatis a-

page.notes: Long s is printed as f in the running text and transcribed as s. The large initial S of the first paragraph is included in the first word. The word "prapositi-ones" is read from the printed "prapofiti-ones" and is doubtful; the first letters may be "praepositi-" or "prepositi-". The marginal note "adversariorum" is partly cut off in the scan and reads "adversarie/rum" with a line break; the reading is doubtful. The handwritten or stamped "674" at top right is not printed text and is left out. The catchword "alicu-" is the start of the next page's first word, given as printed.
